questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase. **

Give somebody a ring

options.text: Inform about the death of a loved one
Trap somebody in a difficult relationship

questions.solution:
Ans: Call someone on the telephone

The phrase ‘give somebody a ring’ means to call someone on the telephone, as specified in Option 3. An example sentence is: ‘As soon as I saw my result, I gave my school principal a ring’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3) **i.e. **'Arrogant'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fustian : (भारी-भरकम)** - Pompous or pretentious speech or writing.

 
 
• **Example:** His speech was full of fustian.

• From the above examples, it is clear that **Fustian **and **Arrogant **are similar to each other.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Arrogant'.

• **Example:** He was a timid child.
 
 
 
• **Courteous : (विनीत)** - Polite, respectful, or considerate in manner.
 
 
• **Example: **She is very courteous.

Such are the strata which we

X -species as those now living in the Mediterranean

Y -meet within the south of Sicily, filled

Z -with shells for the most part of the same
questions.solution:

Sol: The first sentence Y as the word ‘strata’, which means ‘a class of people according to their social status’, are seen in the ‘south of Sicily’. Also, Z comes after Y as ‘filled with shells’ is possible only then. Thus, YZX is the correct combination, as seen only in Option 4.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Vigilance
questions.solution:
Ans: Indifference

Vigilance is the state of keeping careful watch for possible dangers or difficulties. On the other hand, indifference is a state of lack of interest or concern for something. Hence, the two words have opposite meanings. Diligence means careful and persistent work, acuity means sharpness or keenness of thought and circumspection means the quality of being wary and unwilling to take risks.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

The movie critic wrote a sarcastic review.

options.text: A sarcastic review is written by the movie critic.
A review which is sarcastic was written by the movie critic.
A review which is sarcastic is written by the movie critic.
A sarcastic review was written by the movie critic.

questions.solution:
Ans: *A sarcastic review was written by the movie critic.*

Sol: Sentence 1 uses an incorrect tense for the helping verb as it converts the sentence to the present tense. Sentence 2 changes the structure of the sentence by unnecessarily expanding ‘sarcastic review’ and Sentence 3 combines the above two mistakes. Only Sentence 4 uses the correct tense of the sentence and preserves the structure, making it the correct Passive voice.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in ****Indirect****/Direct speech. **

The trainee asked his boss, "Shall I email this letter again, Sir?"

options.text: The trainee asked his boss politely if he shall email that letter again.
The trainee asked his boss politely if he should email that letter again, sir.
The trainee asked his boss politely if he shall email that letter again, sir.
The trainee asked his boss politely if he should email that letter again.

questions.solution:
Ans: The trainee asked his boss politely if he should email that letter again.

Sol: Sentence 1 does not convert ‘shall’ into ‘should’ when changing into reported tense, while Sentences 2 and 3 use the word ‘sir’, when ‘boss’ has been used previously, making the sentence incorrect. Only Option 4 changes the direct speech into the past tense and converts the pronouns properly. This makes Option 4 the only correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Someone must **(being)** killed.
questions.solution:
Ans: have been

Sol: The use of ‘must’ suggests that the course of action to be taken is sure. When used with the perfect tense, ‘must’ indicates a matter of fact or something that must be done in any case. In this case, the action of killing someone was done. Thus, Option 1 is the correct choice. The correct sentence is: ‘Someone must have been killed’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

At this moment that (1)/ terrible door burst noisily open and (2)/ banged for the wall. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Bang means a strike or puts down forcefully or noisily against or on something. The word ‘for’ in the third part of the sentence makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. The correct sentence is: ‘At this moment that terrible door burst noisily open and banged against the wall.’
